prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app product UI comp, 16:10 landscape canvas
Primary request: Create a single shippable-looking screen for an EPL season pick optimization application called “EPL Pick Optimizer”, design direction “The Preparation Room”. This must read unmistakably as a serious predictive modeling tool for choosing one Premier League team each matchweek while preserving future options, not as a poster, landing page, betting site, odds board, casino, or editorial illustration.

Scene/backdrop: Full-frame desktop application interface. Warm analysis-paper workspace (#F2EFE7) with subtle ruled annotations, fine hairline dividers, pencil-like calculation marks, restrained ebonized wood (#191B1F) framing at the far left and bottom, as if a grandmaster’s opening-preparation desk translated into product UI. Flat colors only, absolutely no gradients.

Layout and hierarchy:
- Compact top utility bar, not a giant title: left wordmark “EPL PICK OPTIMIZER”; center context “2026–27  /  MATCHWEEK 1”; right compact status “MODEL READY” and “UPDATED 08:42”.
- Narrow left navigation rail on charcoal/ebonized wood with small labels “PREPARATION”, “SEASON LINE”, “COMMITTED”, “MODEL”. “PREPARATION” is selected with a cobalt marker.
- Main center takes roughly 58% width and begins with a restrained eyebrow “WEEKLY DECISION” then heading “Choose this week’s line” and small explanatory line “Ranked by total season value · one selection required”.
- Central weekly candidate decision table is the visual focus. Columns: “RANK”, “CANDIDATE”, “WIN PROB.”, “EXPECTED PTS”, “SEASON COST”, “AFFECTS”. Exactly three ranked rows:
  1. “Arsenal vs Coventry” — “74%” — “2.34” — “−0.08” — “MW 12”
  2. “Man City vs Bournemouth” — “71%” — “2.21” — “−0.19” — “MW 8”
  3. “Liverpool vs Nott’m Forest” — “68%” — “2.10” — “−0.31” — “MW 15”
  Make Arsenal row selected with a precise cobalt outline, a small filled radio control, and a tiny annotation “engine choice”. Do not use club crests or invented logos.
- Below the table, include a concise engine-note strip reading “+0.11 season EV vs Man City · preserves City for MW 8”.
- Prominent but proportionate primary button at lower center-right reading exactly “Commit Arsenal”, solid cobalt with square-ish 6px corners. Nearby secondary text control “Review assumptions”.
- Right future-impact panel around 26% width, titled “FUTURE IMPACT” with heading “If Arsenal is selected”. Show compact comparison “Season EV  43.82  →  43.74”, “Cost this move  −0.08”, then a vertical continuation line with three future weeks: “MW 8  Man City vs Brentford  72%”, “MW 12  Liverpool at Leeds  69%”, “MW 15  Arsenal used · line reroutes”. Connect nodes with thin cobalt and muted-red notation lines, like chess engine variations. Include a small amber annotation “best remaining line”.
- Along the bottom and wrapping slightly into the left side, create a continuous horizontal “SEASON MOVE TREE” ribbon, not separate cards. It shows connected week nodes and alternate branches: “MW1 ARS” selected, then “MW2 CHE”, “MW3 TOT”, “MW4 NEW”, continuing to “MW8 MCI”, “MW12 LIV”, “MW15 reroute”. Use precise monospaced notation, thin branches, one muted-red displaced node, and an amber active-line marker.
- Include a small footnote on the paper: “Selection previews the optimized remaining season before commit.”

Style/medium: Realistic high-fidelity product UI, pixel-precise and implementation-ready, not concept art. Editorial Swiss information design meets chess engine analysis software and a grandmaster’s annotated opening notebook. Dense but calm, serious, tactile, legible, with practical affordances and restrained depth.
Typography: Dark charcoal serif for the small main heading only, condensed uppercase sans-serif for section labels, neutral sans-serif for table content, monospaced numerals and engine notation. Text must be crisp and readable.
Color palette: analysis paper #F2EFE7, charcoal #191B1F, cobalt #2C5C9F, amber #D79B35, muted red #A74B42; a little off-white and gray ink only.
Materials/textures: Subtle real paper tooth, faint pencil marginalia, hairline ink rules, ebonized wood grain used only as a restrained frame/rail. No glossy glassmorphism.
Interaction implied: selecting a candidate immediately previews the future season line in the right panel and bottom move-tree ribbon. The selected Arsenal state must be unmistakable.
Composition/framing: Straight-on, edge-to-edge 16:10 desktop viewport, no browser chrome, no monitor/device frame, no perspective tilt, no surrounding room or hands. Entire UI visible.
Text (verbatim): “EPL PICK OPTIMIZER”, “2026–27”, “MATCHWEEK 1”, “MODEL READY”, “UPDATED 08:42”, “PREPARATION”, “SEASON LINE”, “COMMITTED”, “MODEL”, “WEEKLY DECISION”, “Choose this week’s line”, “Ranked by total season value · one selection required”, “RANK”, “CANDIDATE”, “WIN PROB.”, “EXPECTED PTS”, “SEASON COST”, “AFFECTS”, “Arsenal vs Coventry”, “74%”, “2.34”, “−0.08”, “MW 12”, “Man City vs Bournemouth”, “71%”, “2.21”, “−0.19”, “MW 8”, “Liverpool vs Nott’m Forest”, “68%”, “2.10”, “−0.31”, “MW 15”, “engine choice”, “+0.11 season EV vs Man City · preserves City for MW 8”, “Commit Arsenal”, “Review assumptions”, “FUTURE IMPACT”, “If Arsenal is selected”, “Season EV 43.82 → 43.74”, “Cost this move −0.08”, “MW 8 Man City vs Brentford 72%”, “MW 12 Liverpool at Leeds 69%”, “MW 15 Arsenal used · line reroutes”, “best remaining line”, “SEASON MOVE TREE”, “MW1 ARS”, “MW2 CHE”, “MW3 TOT”, “MW4 NEW”, “MW8 MCI”, “MW12 LIV”, “MW15 reroute”, “Selection previews the optimized remaining season before commit.”
Constraints: UI mockup, not poster. Preserve the exact candidate names and numeric data. Practical, accessible contrast and visible selected state. No giant title. No generic bento grid. No invented performance claims. No charts suggesting gambling. No bookmaker language, odds, currency, trophy, stadium photo, football action photo, casino imagery, decorative footballs, gradients, neon, excessive rounded cards, glassmorphism, large hero illustration, watermark, or extra unrelated text.
